title: Aerofy Systems - Model context, multilingual & tooling evaluation
summary: Initial technical discovery to map Aerofy Systems' requirements for LLM-powered cockpit assistant: high-context docs (20k+ tokens), Spanish/Portuguese support, tool-calling for live DB lookups and flight-plan actions. Discussed tradeoffs between Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, and Private (VPC/on-prem), plus open-model candidates and quantization/latency implications.
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment
model selection: open models (LlamaX, Mistral, Falcon variants)
action_items: Jordan Lee - Share model performance spreadsheet and estimated token pricing by model/quant profile - Due 2026-06-04
Priya Raman - Propose an initial benchmark plan and test prompts (Spanish/Portuguese) - Due 2026-06-07
Ethan Park - Provide sample logs and a low-sensitivity dataset for latency benchmarking (sanitized) - Due 2026-06-10
next_steps: Jordan to send pricing + perf spreadsheet
Schedule a 60-min benchmark kickoff with Aerofy infra and ML (w/ Dedicated config) week of 6/8
Customer to confirm internal decision timeline and procurement contacts
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-06-01 15:00 UTC | Duration 48m | Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Marcus Holt (CTO, Aerofy), Sofia Alvarez (ML Eng), Ethan Park (Infra), Lina Gomez (Product)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. I'm Jordan from Redwood, and with me is Priya, our SE. Quick intros?
[00:12] Marcus: Marcus here, CTO at Aerofy Systems. We build avionics data pipelines and cockpit assistance, looking to add an LLM-backed assistant for dispatch and quick-flight-plan checks.
[00:23] Sofia: Hi, Sofia - ML engineer. I'll own the model evaluation and latency questions.
[00:28] Ethan: Ethan, infra. I'm primarily worried about VPC connectivity and throughput.
[00:32] Lina: Lina - product. Focused on UX and multilingual support.
[00:36] Priya: Great, thanks. Quick agenda: map out requirements (context length, languages), go over deployment options (Hosted/Dedicated/Private), and talk model candidates and tool-calling.

[02:05] Marcus: I'll kick off with the big constraint — we routinely need to reference long flight logs, maintenance docs, and prior comms. Effective context for some flows is north of 15k tokens, sometimes 20k-plus. Can Redwood support that?
[02:27] Priya: Yes, we support model variants with extended context — there are tradeoffs. Hosted supports many long-context open models we curate; Dedicated gives you reserved capacity and can push larger KV cache sizes; Private is for air-gapped, but requires heavier ops. For 20k tokens, throughput/latency will depend on model and quantization settings.
[03:01] Sofia: Do you have specific models in mind? We're leaning open-source for data control — thinking LLaMAX-40b or Mistral-XL-type variants. Also evaluating Falcon-40b-instruct.
[03:18] Jordan: Good candidates. Our catalog has performance profiles for those — LLaMAX tends to have strong long-context perf, Mistral variants are cost-effective, and Falcon sometimes needs more mem but can be quantized. We'll share a spreadsheet with token/sec and latency estimates across Hosted and Dedicated.

[04:10] Ethan: On infra — if we go Hosted, how does VPC peering work? We need private endpoints for tool-calling into our internal flight DBs.
[04:22] Priya: For Hosted we offer secure egress via customer-managed VPC peering and a private connector — you'll get a private endpoint and can restrict IP ranges. For fully private, we'd install our control plane in your VPC or on-prem bundle; that gives you zero egress. There's a middle ground: Dedicated in a customer-owned VPC.
[04:48] Ethan: Okay, and audit logs? We must keep immutable audit trails for any production calls.
[04:55] Jordan: We provide audit logs in the Console with retention options; enterprise packages can push logs to your SIEM. SOC 2 is standard; we also support SAML SSO and RBAC.

[06:10] Lina: Multilingual — Spanish and Portuguese are priorities. We saw hallucination issues in Spanish with some smaller models. What's your recommendation?
[06:22] Priya: Generally pick an instruction-tuned multilingual model or run an ensemble. For Spanish/Portuguese we often recommend models fine-tuned on multilingual corpora or using a larger LLM with high-quality tokenization. Also, we can run targeted evals to quantify hallucination rates on your prompt set.
[06:41] Sofia: Can Redwood run those evals for us? We have labeled examples and a set of real user prompts.
[06:46] Jordan: Yes, Redwood Optimize can run evals and produce quality regressions tied to prompt sets. Priya can propose an eval plan — ideally a mix of synthetic prompts and your labeled set.

[08:33] Marcus: Tool-calling: we want the assistant to do DB reads for plane status and to trigger actions like 'clear for dispatch' which should call internal APIs. What's the security model?
[08:45] Priya: For tool-calling we support function-style structured outputs and webhooks. In Hosted we proxy calls through secure connectors; for Dedicated/Private you can host the runtimes inside your network. We also offer signed requests, short-lived credentials, and per-route RBAC so only certain prompts can trigger mutation-level calls.
[09:06] Ethan: So in Hosted there's still an egress path that touches Redwood infra? We can't have anything unencrypted leaving the VPC for certain workflows.
[09:15] Jordan: Correct — Hosted uses our control plane but can be configured with encryption and private peering. If you require zero third-party network hops, Private deployment or on-prem package is the recommended path.

[11:20] Sofia: On latency — interactive cockpit flows need sub-400ms token latencies for short prompts; for long-context summarization we can tolerate higher. How do you set latency SLAs?
[11:33] Priya: We publish model-specific latency profiles. Dedicated offers predictable latency because of reserved GPU pools and autoscaling policies tuned to your traffic. Hosted has shared pools but tiered guarantees; for strict SLAs you typically pick Dedicated. We can run a benchmark with your payloads to give better numbers.

[13:05] Marcus: Cost — what's the unit economics if we push 20k-context requests frequently?
[13:13] Jordan: Unit cost depends on tokens, model size, and quantization. Long-context drastically increases compute; caching/prefix caching helps if you reuse history. Our Optimize tool suggests batching and KV cache to reduce cost — that spreadsheet will include estimates for typical reuse rates.

[14:02] Lina: Any gotchas with quantization and multilingual quality? Sometimes 4-bit quant causes grammar regression in non-English.
[14:15] Priya: Yes, 4-bit quantization can affect generation quality in underrepresented languages. We usually recommend controlled quant profiles: keep the critical layers in higher precision or use mixed-precision pipelines for Spanish/Portuguese-critical routes. Those are configurable per-model in Dedicated/Private.

[16:00] Sofia: About model updates — how do we pin versions and rollback if a new model regresses?
[16:08] Jordan: Console supports model pinning, canary rollouts, A/B tests, and automatic fallback policies. You can pin the model version at route-level and define rollback policies if eval metrics drop.

[17:30] Marcus: For open models, what's Redwood's role in maintaining performance? If we rely on community forks, who handles kernel selection and optimization?
[17:44] Priya: Redwood's runtime includes kernel selection and optimized execution for many open architectures. For Dedicated/Private we manage the runtime and kernel selection in the control plane; we can also bring optimizations for specific hardware — e.g., sequences with attention optimizations for long context. If you need custom kernels we can collaborate via an eng engagement.

[19:25] Ethan: Networking: if we choose Dedicated in our cloud account, can we use our KMS for key management?
[19:33] Priya: Yes, Dedicated and Private support KMS integration (customer-managed keys) and HSM options for on-prem.

[21:40] Sofia: Let's talk models more concretely. Could you sketch a shortlist for our use-case?
[21:48] Jordan: Shortlist: LLaMAX-40b-long (long context tuned), Mistral-XL-7B-instruct with extended context patch (cost-effective), Falcon-40b-instruct (good instruction following), and a 70B open variant if you need top-tier multilingual. We'll annotate tradeoffs in the spreadsheet — e.g., Mistral for cost, LLaMAX for long-context stability, Falcon as a middle ground.

[23:02] Lina: Any recommendation for tool-calling safety? We need to prevent accidental dispatch commands.
[23:11] Priya: Multi-step guardrails: 1) structured output schema so the model returns a vetted payload, 2) server-side validation and a human-in-loop approval step for critical mutations, 3) per-user RBAC and route-level rate limiting. We can demo a policy that requires a 2-step confirm for 'clear for dispatch'.

[25:00] Marcus: Benchmarking — we'd want Redwood to run a pilot: 1) run 500 sample prompts with our sanitized logs in Spanish/Portuguese, 2) measure latency and token cost across 3 models, 3) run tool-calling scenarios in a sandbox. Can you do that?
[25:18] Jordan: Yes, that's our typical pilot. Priya will own the test plan and we'll need sanitized examples from you. Expect a 2-week turnaround for initial runs.

[27:10] Ethan: Data residency question — some of our customers require EU-only data handling. Does Redwood host in EU regions for Hosted?
[27:20] Priya: We have hosted regions in EU and NA; for EU-only you can pick an EU region and restrict routing. For strict residency with no third-party access, Private is the option.

[29:50] Sofia: Regarding streaming and partial responses — we need partial outputs while the model is summarizing long logs. How's that handled with long context?
[30:02] Priya: We support streaming with prefix caching — you can stream tokens while the KV cache continues to build. For very long contexts there may be slightly higher startup latency, but the streaming continues as tokens are generated.

[32:40] Marcus: Are there known multi-model strategies to reduce hallucinations? We saw ensembles help.
[32:50] Priya: Yes: reranking (embed-based retrieval then rerank candidates), retrieval-augmented generation with gold snippets, and model ensembles for critical reads. Redwood supports retrieval integrations and reranking pipelines.

[34:12] Lina: Ops question — what's the rollout process if we start on Hosted then move to Dedicated later?
[34:20] Jordan: We design the API abstraction so routes and prompts remain the same; you can pin models and switch the backend in the Console. Migration steps include capacity planning, a short validation window, and DNS/VPC updates if needed. We've done several migrations for customers with no API changes.

[36:45] Ethan: One more infra nit — can we run on our preferred GPU instance types? We have credits with a cloud provider and want to use A100s.
[36:55] Priya: Dedicated supports custom instance types; for Private/on-prem you control hardware. If you want A100 pools, we can size accordingly. We'll capture exact GPU types in the benchmark plan.

[38:50] Sofia: About logging and observability — token-level cost breakdowns and per-route latency traces are must-haves.
[38:58] Jordan: Console provides token-level cost breakdowns and tracing hooks; you can also export traces to your observability backend.

[40:12] Marcus: Any legal/compliance concerns — we will need a DPA and data processing terms for EU customers.
[40:20] Jordan: We have standard DPAs and can provide SOC 2, ISO attestations on request. For Private deployments we can put the control plane behind your auditors.

[42:00] Lina: OK, this is super helpful. Can we get the pricing and benchmark plan as a package?
[42:07] Jordan: Yes — action items: I'll send the model perf/pricing spreadsheet, Priya will send a 2-week benchmark plan, and Ethan will send sample sanitized logs.

[43:05] Marcus: Timeline — we want an internal decision by end of June. Is that feasible?
[43:12] Jordan: Yes — pilot results and pricing should land early-mid June and fit your timeline.

[45:00] Priya: I'll follow up with a proposed schedule for the benchmark kickoff and list of required artifacts.
[45:06] Jordan: Thanks everyone. Quick recap in chat: Jordan sends spreadsheet, Priya sends test plan, Ethan shares sanitized logs. We'll schedule the kickoff.

[46:10] Marcus: Thanks, talk soon.
[46:15] Sofia: Thanks all.

Meeting end.

Notes: minor transcription artifacts: 'KV cash' heard at 02:27 twice; 'quantizashun' noted at 14:15; some speaker bleed between Marcus and Ethan around 36:55.
